cards.text: Sargon, king of Assyria, sends his chief commander to Ashdod, and the commander attacks the city and captures it. But before that year ever comes, the LORD has already given Isaiah son of Amoz an assignment. And friend, this one is NOT in anybody's job description.

cards.question: The LORD tells Isaiah to go and take two things off. What are they?

answers.text: The sackcloth from his waist and his sandals
The cloak from his shoulders and his belt
The ring from his hand and his turban

cards.question: When the LORD tells Isaiah to take off his sackcloth and sandals, Isaiah pushes back and asks for a different sign.

cards.text: No arguing. No "LORD, can we talk about this?" Isaiah just does it, walking around naked and barefoot.

cards.question: Isaiah keeps going naked and barefoot for ___ years.

cards.text: THREE YEARS. Friend, I can't wait twelve minutes on an oven timer without opening the door six times. Then the LORD speaks, and He calls him "My servant Isaiah."

cards.question: The LORD says Isaiah's three years of going naked and barefoot are a sign and omen. Against who?

cards.text: Here's what the sign points to. Just as Isaiah went naked and barefoot, captives from Egypt and Cush will be led away naked and barefoot too.

cards.question: Captives from Egypt and Cush will be led away naked and barefoot. Who leads them away?
The king of Assyria leads away only the young people of Egypt and Cush.
The captives are led away naked and barefoot, and the LORD says it will bring Egypt ___.

cards.text: And friend, Egypt and Cush won't be the only ones hanging their heads.

cards.question: Besides Egypt and Cush, who ends up dismayed and ashamed?

answers.text: Those who made them their hope and boast
The soldiers who march for Assyria
The priests who serve in Jerusalem

cards.text: Then the people of this coastland speak up. They look at what has happened to their source of hope, the ones they fled to for help.

cards.question: The people of this coastland fled to their source of hope for help and deliverance. Deliverance from who?
The coastland people see what has happened to their source of hope. What do they ask?

answers.text: Who will be our king now
Where can we hide our gold

cards.text: And that's where it ends, with the coastland asking how they can escape. Friend, I asked that same question from the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, so nobody's laughing at them over here.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "My servant Isaiah.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This is Isaiah's first appearance, but the card only gives his father's name. It never says who Isaiah is (a prophet). A baker who doesn't know Isaiah gets no identification.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke's core action doesn't match the fact. Isaiah keeps up a hard, exposed act of obedience for three years. The oven-timer comparison is about being impatient while waiting, which is a different action.

rule.text: Find the core action in the fact: running away, waiting, being outnumbered, preparing, being surprised. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "Egypt and Cush won't be the only ones hanging their heads" says Cush is shamed. The text names only Egypt's shame (Isaiah 20:4). Verse 5 says those who trusted Cush and Egypt will be dismayed and ashamed. It never says Cush itself is.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "Besides Egypt and Cush, who ends up dismayed and ashamed?" assumes Egypt and Cush are dismayed and ashamed. Isaiah 20:5 gives that only to those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast, and the text never says Cush is ashamed.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The right answer is the exact BSB line "How then can we escape", with its biblical "then." The wrong answers are plain modern phrasing ("Who will be our king now", "Where can we hide our gold"). The right answer sounds more like the Bible than the others.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The last story card restates what card 16 already answered ("with the coastland asking how they can escape") and tells no new part of the passage. It's a recap carrying a joke, not a step forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
